stories.title: MMFlash speeds up speculative decoding for vision-language models
stories.summary: A new method, MMFlash, extends speculative decoding to multimodal models by measuring how much each token depends on visual input, addressing a gap left by text-only drafters like DFlash.
stories.more: Speculative decoding normally uses a lightweight drafter to propose tokens that a larger target model verifies in parallel, but prior block-proposing drafters such as DFlash focused on text only. The authors introduce a metric of token-level visual dependence, based on the KL divergence between next-token predictions with and without visual input. They find that acceptance of drafted tokens varies with how visually dependent a token is, motivating a multimodal-aware approach. The excerpt does not give MMFlash's measured speedup over text-only baselines.

stories.title: Paper analyzes how Looped Transformers reuse computation via residuals
stories.summary: A new paper examines Looped Transformers, which cut parameter count by reusing shared blocks, and argues that residual connections determine how repeated computation's results get reused.
stories.more: Looped Transformers save parameters by applying the same blocks repeatedly, but the authors note that parameter sharing alone doesn't decide how later steps reuse earlier results. Taking a 'depth-memory' view of residual connections, they analyze which representation is stored after each block and how later reads weight it. They point out that a full block's output mixes its input with its new update, so reweighting the output also reweights history already carried in the input. The excerpt does not detail the paper's proposed fix or its experimental results.

stories.title: New benchmark tests text-to-SQL systems' ability to reuse past queries
stories.summary: A new benchmark, HARE, measures whether text-to-SQL systems can adapt earlier queries over the same database to answer a new, related question, rather than treating each question in isolation.
stories.more: Most text-to-SQL benchmarks evaluate each natural-language question independently, ignoring cases where an earlier query over the same database could supply useful joins or calculations for a later one. The paper introduces HARE (History-AwaRe Text-to-SQL BEnchmark) to measure both the accuracy and the cost of adapting historical SQL to new questions. HARE comprises 1,600 requests built from a fixed pool of 823 verified queries. The excerpt does not report how existing systems perform on the benchmark.

stories.title: JVT simplifies pixel-space video diffusion with a plain transformer
stories.summary: A new model, JVT (Just Video Transformer), generates video directly in pixel space using a large-patch DiT-style transformer, skipping the pretrained autoencoders and specialized architectures earlier methods relied on.
stories.more: Direct diffusion modeling of raw, high-dimensional video has typically required specialized architectures such as pretrained autoencoders, auxiliary detail networks, cascaded stages or U-Net-style skip connections. JVT instead uses a simple large-patch, DiT-style transformer with none of these additions. The authors systematically study video patch embeddings, register tokens and adaptive layer normalization to settle on its design. The excerpt does not include JVT's generation quality results compared to existing video diffusion methods.

stories.title: Bonbon foundation model shows emergent skills in molecular interactions
stories.summary: Trained on about 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences, the Bonbon foundation model displays emergent zero-shot abilities in predicting molecular mechanism of action and binding sites.
stories.more: The paper extends the idea of emergent capabilities, skills beyond a model's training objective, to multimodal biology. Bonbon is trained on roughly 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequence data. From a single learned representation space, it shows three zero-shot emergent capabilities at different levels of resolution, including mechanism of action at the functional level and binding site location at the residue level. The excerpt does not specify Bonbon's third emergent capability or how it was benchmarked.

stories.title: Datasette 1.0a43 adds streaming export support, nears 1.0
stories.summary: Datasette 1.0a43 adds streaming support for output renderers, including built-in TSV and CSV export, as the 1.0 milestone reaches 53% complete.
stories.more: Simon Willison says he has been leaning on Claude Fable 5.2 to help finish items on Datasette's 1.0 milestone, now 53% complete. The biggest item in this release is streaming support for output renderers, which the built-in TSV and CSV export mechanisms now use as well. Plugins can register themselves as capable of streaming every row of a table in one go via a new Response.stream() method. The release also includes a couple of security fixes, one of which Willison considered serious enough to warrant a GitHub advisory.

stories.title: Datasette 0.65.6 backports fix for a database access control bug
stories.summary: Datasette 0.65.6 backports a security fix from 1.0a43 that could let denied actors download a database registered with a differing route name.
stories.more: The fix addresses an issue where a database registered using add_database(db, name=..., route=...) with a route that differs from its name could be downloaded from /name.db by actors who had been denied access to it. The fix was originally released in 1.0a43 and has now been backported to the 0.65.x branch. The excerpt does not state how long the issue had existed or whether any exploitation was observed.

stories.title: Gamer: a vision-language-action model for long, real-time game play
stories.summary: Researchers introduce Gamer, a generalist agent that combines perception, memory and multi-step reasoning to handle long-horizon tasks in both 2D interfaces and 3D simulated worlds.
stories.more: Gamer is pre-trained on tens of thousands of hours of device-level keyboard and mouse interaction trajectories. Its end-to-end architecture handles perception, memory management and multi-step reasoning in one pipeline. A shared training and deployment pipeline lets it work across conventional 2D graphical interfaces and complex 3D simulated worlds. The excerpt does not specify evaluation results or which games were tested.

stories.title: Paper charts the rise of 'agentic robotics' after GPT-6 Astra's robot wins
stories.summary: A new paper argues that agentic foundation models, following GPT-6 Astra's embodied benchmark wins, are replacing task-specific robot policies with general-purpose systems that perceive, reason and invoke skills in a closed loop.
stories.more: The paper traces agentic robotics to GPT-6 Astra's agentic harness, which matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks within weeks of release. Rather than training a separate policy per task family, an agentic robotic system applies one foundation model across open-world embodied tasks. It works in a closed loop: observing its environment, interpreting user intent, reasoning about the task, and invoking and chaining skills to complete it. The excerpt does not detail which benchmarks were used or how broadly the approach generalizes.
